A component re-renders for only a few reasons: its own state changed, its parent re-rendered, a context it reads changed, or a hook it uses triggered an update. "Too many" re-renders almost always trace back to one of these causes. ## 1. Parent re-renders (the most common cause) By default, when a parent renders, every child renders too, even if its props are identical. **Fixes:** - Wrap the child in `React.memo` so it skips rendering when props are shallow-equal. - Move state down so it lives in the smallest component that needs it and fewer components sit under it. - Lift content up by passing expensive subtrees as `children`. Elements created by a higher component keep the same reference, so React skips them: ```jsx function Wrapper({ children }) { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return
setCount(c => c + 1)}>{children}
; // children don't re-render } ``` ## 2. Unstable prop references defeat `memo` Objects, arrays, and functions created inline are new on every render, so `React.memo` sees changed props. ```jsx save(id)} items={list.filter(isActive)} /> ``` **Fixes:** - Use `useMemo` for objects and arrays, and `useCallback` for functions. - Hoist constants out of the component (`const STYLE = { margin: 8 }`). - Pass primitives instead of objects where you can (`userId` rather than `user`). - If you're on React 19 with the React Compiler, it memoizes these automatically. ## 3. Context value changes Every consumer re-renders when the provider's `value` changes identity, including when it's a fresh object literal each render. ```jsx {/* new object every render */} ``` **Fixes:** - Memoize the value: `useMemo(() => ({ user, setUser }), [user])`. - Split contexts, for example state vs. dispatch, or fast-changing vs. slow-changing data. - For fine-grained subscriptions, use a store with selectors (Zustand, Redux, Jotai, or `useSyncExternalStore`). ## 4. Components defined inside components ```jsx function Parent() { const Row = () =>
; // new component type every render return ; } ``` This is worse than a re-render: React unmounts and remounts `Row` each time, losing its state and DOM. **Fix:** define components at module scope and pass data through props. ## 5. Effects that set state An effect that calls `setState` causes a second render, and an unstable dependency turns that into a loop. ```jsx useEffect(() => { setFiltered(items.filter(fn)); }, [items, fn]); // extra render every time ``` **Fixes:** - Compute derived data during render (`const filtered = useMemo(...)`) instead of mirroring it into state. - Stabilize the dependencies, or depend on primitives. - Check for missing dependency arrays, since an effect without one runs after every render. ## 6. Overly broad store or hook subscriptions Selecting a whole store, or returning a new object from a selector, re-renders on any change. Custom hooks have the same problem: any state inside them re-renders every component that uses them. ```jsx const { a, b } = useStore(s => ({ a: s.a, b: s.b })); // new object each time ``` **Fixes:** - Select the smallest slice you need, with separate selectors. - Pass a shallow equality function (`useShallow` in Zustand, `shallowEqual` in Redux). - Split hooks that bundle unrelated state. ## 7. Unstable or misused keys `key={Math.random()}` remounts every item on every render. `key={index}` on a list that reorders causes wrong state reuse and extra work. **Fix:** use stable, unique IDs from your data. ## 8. High-frequency state updates Scroll, mouse-move, and keystroke handlers that set state high in the tree re-render everything below them. **Fixes:** - Keep that state local to a leaf component. - Throttle or debounce the updates. - Use `useRef` for values that don't affect the output. - Use `useDeferredValue` or `useTransition` to deprioritize expensive subtrees. ## 9. Things that aren't real problems - **StrictMode double-rendering:** this is intentional, happens in development only, and isn't present in production. - **Re-renders that are cheap:** a render that produces the same output results in no DOM changes. Don't memoize until you've measured a problem, because `memo`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback` have their own cost. ## How to find the actual cause 1. **React DevTools Profiler:** enable "Record why each component rendered" in its settings, record an interaction, and it will tell you whether props, state, hooks, or the parent triggered each render. 2. **"Highlight updates when components render":** this DevTools setting gives you a quick visual read on what is rendering. 3. **`why-did-you-render`:** this library logs avoidable re-renders with the specific prop that changed. 4. **A temporary `console.log`** in the component body, or a `useEffect` that diffs the previous and current props. Start with the Profiler: fix whichever component is actually slow, using the cause it reports, rather than applying memoization everywhere.
